name: What must pass before the next step: mandated step order in regulated processes
description: The mandated order of steps in multi-step regulated processes, from the authority that enforces the order: which inspection or filing must be approved before the next one may happen, what may not proceed until it passes, and the deadline attached to it. One record is one step in one authority's published sequence. Covers municipal building inspection sequences (the rough-in must pass before the wall closes; no concrete before the footing inspection) and the US import Importer Security Filing chain (ISF no later than 24 hours before lading; flexible filings finalised no later than 24 hours before arrival; cargo release withheld without an ISF). Answers 'did I need an inspection before drywall', 'what order do building inspections happen in', 'when does the ISF have to be filed', and 'what happens if the ISF is late'. The sequence is usually published only as prose on the enforcing authority's own page, one jurisdiction at a time; no comparison table exists anywhere.
licence: Facts extracted from the freely published pages of the authorities that enforce each sequence — municipal building departments and US Customs and Border Protection — with a short attributed quote and a link back. Inspection order and filing deadlines are public regulatory facts. No source page used carries a restrictive notice; US federal documents are public domain.

records.step_name: Duty to Request a Final Inspection and Obtain Final Approval
records.prerequisite: Upon completion of the work described in the permit application and on the approved construction documents
records.hold_point: the permit holder must request a final inspection and obtain final approval before any occupancy of the building or structure may occur
records.source_quote: 10. Duty to Request a Final Inspection and Obtain Final Approval Upon completion of the work described in the permit application and on the approved construction documents, the permit holder must request a final inspection and obtain final approval before any occupancy of the building or structure may occur. Failure of the permit holder to obtain final approval constitutes a violation of the Building Code and subjects the permit holder to penalties as set forth in Section 116.4.

The following items should be in place and visible for inspection: Pipes Chimneys and vents Flashing for roofs, chimneys and wall openings Insulation baffles All lintels required to be bolted to the framing for support shall not be covered by any interior or exterior wall or ceiling finish materials before approval.

records.step_name: Appendix D stand-alone continuous ISF bonds
records.deadline: in advance of the filing of an ISF
records.source_quote: Appendix D stand-alone continuous ISF bonds must be submitted to, and approved by CBP’s Office of Finance in advance of the filing of an ISF. Once approved, CBP will record the bond information within the Automated Commercial System (ACS) and issue a unique bond identification number.

records.prerequisite: Without the bill of lading number, the ISF cannot be matched to a customs manifest
records.deadline: 24 hours prior to the cargo being laden on a vessel destined to the United States
records.source_quote: The ISF Importer must obtain the bill of lading number, as it is an integral part of the security filing. Without the bill of lading number, the ISF cannot be matched to a customs manifest. The bill of lading number is part of the customs manifest information that is already required to be presented to CBP by the carrier or automated Non-Vessel Operating Common Carrier (NVOCC) 24 hours prior to the cargo being laden on a vessel destined to the United States.

records.step_name: change the in-bond entry into a consumption entry
records.prerequisite: Such permission would only be granted upon receipt by Customs and Border Protection (CBP) of a complete Importer Security Filing as required by part 149 of this chapter
records.source_quote: “[permission to] change the in-bond entry into a consumption entry must be obtained from the port director of the port of origin. Such permission would only be granted upon receipt by Customs and Border Protection (CBP) of a complete Importer Security Filing as required by part 149 of this chapter.”

records.prerequisite: All data is present and is based upon the best information available at the time of the filing
records.source_quote: CT - Compliant Transaction – All data is present and is based upon the best information available at the time of the filing; no special flexibility rules apply. If CT is used, the ISF can be updated if necessary, but CBP does not necessarily expect to see updates for these filings. CT is also used to finalize a FR, FT or FX filing.

records.prerequisite: a bond can be secured in time for the filing
records.source_quote: Early filing of ISF is encouraged as it allows more time to make amendments and it is a good practice to ensure that a bond can be secured in time for the filing.

records.prerequisite: the ISF must be updated as soon as better information becomes available
records.deadline: no later than 24 hours prior to arrival
records.source_quote: FR - Flexible Range – A range of data for the Manufacturer, and/or Ship To Party, and/or Country of Origin, and/or Commodity HTSUS number has been provided. In these cases, the ISF must be updated as soon as better information becomes available, but in any event no later than 24 hours prior to arrival. If FR is used, CBP will expect a timely update.

records.deadline: prior to lading aboard a vessel destined to the United States
records.source_quote: Similarly, for FROB, the required elements must be submitted prior to lading aboard a vessel destined to the United States.

records.prerequisite: The ISF must be updated as soon as better information becomes available
records.deadline: no later than 24 hours prior to arrival
records.source_quote: FT - Flexible Timing – The CS (consolidator name/address) and/or the LG (stuffing location) has not been provided. The ISF must be updated as soon as better information becomes available, but in any event no later than 24 hours prior to arrival. If FT is used, CBP will expect to receive a timely update.

records.step_name: FX - Flexible Range and Flexible Timing
records.prerequisite: The ISF must be updated as soon as better information becomes available
records.deadline: no later than 24 hours prior to arrival
records.source_quote: FX - Flexible Range and Flexible Timing - A range of data as described in FR has been provided and the CS (consolidator name/address) and/or LG (stuffing location) have not been provided. The ISF must be updated as soon as better information becomes available, but in any event no later than 24 hours prior to arrival. If FX is used, CBP will expect a timely update.

records.step_name: ISF-10 will be replacing the existing ISF-5
records.prerequisite: an active ISF-5 filing must already exist for this shipment against the same bill of lading number (i.e., lowest AMS bill of lading number) in order for this new filing to be valid
records.source_quote: In these instances, a new ISF-10 must be created and ISF Submission Type “3” must be selected to denote that an ISF-10 will be replacing the existing ISF-5. Note that an active ISF-5 filing must already exist for this shipment against the same bill of lading number (i.e., lowest AMS bill of lading number) in order for this new filing to be valid.

records.deadline: no later than 24 hours before the cargo is laden aboard a vessel destined to the United States
records.source_quote: For ISF elements that must be submitted no later than 24 hours before the cargo is laden aboard the vessel at the foreign port, the elements must be submitted no later than 24 hours before the cargo is laden aboard a vessel destined to the United States.

records.prerequisite: Break-bulk cargo that is exempt from the timing requirements of the 24 Hour Rule are automatically exempt from the timing requirements of the ISF filing
records.deadline: no later than 24 hours prior to arrival
records.source_quote: Break-bulk cargo that is exempt from the timing requirements of the 24 Hour Rule are automatically exempt from the timing requirements of the ISF filing. ISFs for break-bulk cargo that are exempt from the timing requirements of the 24 Hour Rule must be filed no later than 24 hours prior to arrival.

records.deadline: at least 24 hours prior to the vessel departure
records.source_quote: H. Late ISFs 1. If an ISF is filed the day of the vessel sail date, will there be a fine or enforcement of some kind? Because the ISF is required at least 24 hours prior to the vessel departure, a filing that is completed the same day the vessel sails will be considered a violation and it can be expected that CBP will issue a claim for an untimely filing. CBP uses the vessel departure date minus 24 hours to measure timeliness.

records.hold_point: Release of shipments with no associated ISF will be withheld until the ISF is provided
records.source_quote: CBP has been in full enforcement phase of the ISF since July 9, 2013. Release of shipments with no associated ISF will be withheld until the ISF is provided.

records.process: Appendix D stand-alone single transaction ISF bond submission
records.source_quote: Step 1: The ISF Importer, or its agent, must denote the usage of the Appendix D stand- alone single transaction ISF bond on the ISF by identifying bond activity code 16, bond type 9 (single transaction), the valid surety code and the bond reference number.

records.process: Appendix D stand-alone single transaction ISF bond submission
records.prerequisite: After CBP has received and accepted the ISF
records.source_quote: Step 2: After CBP has received and accepted the ISF, the ISF filer will receive a unique ISF transaction number from CBP. The ISF Importer, or its agent, must affix a legible copy of the ISF transaction number (e.g., typed and of a font size 12) onto the Appendix D stand-alone ISF bond.

records.process: Appendix D stand-alone single transaction ISF bond submission
records.deadline: within 12 hours of receipt of the unique ISF transaction number
records.source_quote: Step 3: An electronic copy of the bond containing the unique ISF transaction number must be created in a .pdf or .tif format and e-mailed to the ISF_Bond@cbp.dhs.gov mailbox within 12 hours of receipt of the unique ISF transaction number.

records.deadline: before the goods enter the limits of the port of first arrival in the United States
records.source_quote: The ISF must be amended if there is a change or if more accurate information becomes available before the goods enter the limits of the port of first arrival in the United States.

records.step_name: written permission from the local CBP port director
records.prerequisite: CBP expects the new ISF-10 to be completed electronically prior to seeking the written permission from the local CBP port director
records.source_quote: In terms of the business process, CBP expects the new ISF-10 to be completed electronically prior to seeking the written permission from the local CBP port director. Accordingly, the ISF-10 transaction number needs to be referenced in the written letter to the local port director as part of the request for the change from a shipment type requiring an ISF-5 to shipment type requiring an ISF-10.
